title: -ar/-er/-ir, the I form, comer, tener, vengo

cards.title: Warm-up: more -ar verbs
cards.body: Read the spelling, not the English sound: separate has an a, so separar.

cards.title: Memory hooks
cards.body: Saber (to know) links to savvy and Homo sapiens (the 'wise' one). Venir links to conveniente, 'with coming'.

cards.title: 'To' forms end in r; 'I' forms usually in o
cards.body: Quiero, debo, intento end in -o for 'I'. Irregular verbs, like voy, break the pattern.

cards.title: Three verb types: -ar, -er, -ir
cards.body: Every 'to' form ends in -ar, -er or -ir. The -ation rule gives you many -ar verbs; saber is an -er verb and venir an -ir verb.

cards.title: What is a verb?
cards.body: A verb is a word you can put 'to' in front of: to be, to stay, to go. 'Doing word' doesn't fit 'is', which comes from 'to be'. In Spanish, these 'to' forms end in r.

cards.title: Making the I form: drop the ending, add -o, move the stress
cards.body: Remove -ar/-er/-ir and add -o. The stress moves to the second-to-last syllable: inTENto. This matters: stressing the end (intentó) means 'he tried', a past form you'll meet later.

cards.title: Present for the future
cards.body: If something like mañana already shows it's future, you can just use the present: 'I eat tomorrow' is perfect Spanish. Con (with) comes from confirmar.

examples.es: Voy a comer con Pablo mañana.

cards.title: organizar → organizo
cards.body: The z is s in most places, th in much of Spain.

cards.title: tener = to have; más = more
cards.body: Later = 'more late' = más tarde (link más to massive).

examples.en: I'm going to have it later.

cards.title: -tain = tener
cards.body: English -tain matches Spanish tener: contain → contener, obtain → obtener, sustain → sostener (sus → sos), maintain → mantener, entertain → entretener. Entre means 'between'.

cards.title: tengo, vengo — irregular in a group
cards.body: I have is tengo (a g appears instead of 'teno'). Irregular verbs come in groups: venir does the same, so 'I come' is vengo.

es: Voy a comer con Pablo mañana
practice.why: Future context lets you use the present: como … mañana.

practice.en: I'm going to have it later.
